decision.decision: Do not promote this D2 consumer experiment to the selected full-model baseline. Restore exact D1 main; preserve candidate source, the useful new CUDA test and all positive/negative observations.
decision.reason: The local direct-BF16 path is cheaper in this observation, but neither complete-model window establishes a throughput benefit. This is a baseline-selection decision, not proof that BF16 Top1 is slower, mathematically wrong, or useless on other hardware.

decision.memory_bandwidth_hypothesis: Dominant weight streaming can dilute small suffix/host improvements; no new full-step DRAM saturation measurement was performed. Lower physical traffic/cache reuse improvements remain relevant. Do not blame this candidate on a hardware bottleneck without counters.
decision.next: End this bounded D2 investigation absent a new measured premise; proceed with remaining format/function packages. Retain D1 as the throughput reference and test the current closure at final delivery.

independent_timing_review.method: Independent parsing of original Hyle stderr key/value lines plus stdout final JSON, and original llama peer phase JSON. No author script imports, compilation, GPU execution, new measurement, source changes, or removal of slow samples. Rates calculated per process, then median across exactly three fresh processes per arm.
independent_timing_review.scope: This retained D1 product closure with only the candidate consumer main object replaced; not a rebuild of all current format owners. Image identities below come from original inputs metadata, not a new executable/dependency rehash.

formulas.observed_spread_percent: 100*(max(process_rates)/min(process_rates)-1); descriptive within-arm variability, not a confidence interval or a proven drift mechanism

raw_identity_manifest.selection: Both windows: all09 process result.json/stderr.log/stdout.log, all03 llama-peer-result.json, inputs.json, summary.json. Identity entries are relative path, bytes, sha256; original members remain separately retained.

judgment.observed_result: Candidate medians are lower than baseline in both full-decode and warm7-end windows. Short full -0.94536%, warm -0.70450%; long full -0.81500%, warm -0.82642%. No demonstrated throughput benefit.
judgment.variability: Long baseline full-decode process rates range 98.6670..106.7781 tokens/s (8.22067% max/min spread); current and peer also vary. This is larger than the median candidate/baseline delta. Time ordering is rotated but there is no same-image A/A control or stationarity proof; neither attributing the entire delta to the change nor dismissing it as mere timer resolution is justified.
judgment.correctness_vs_performance: The separately completed three TopK tests and 64 byte-equal vectors establish tested semantic compatibility. Structural reduction to 595 kernels/54 Casts verifies removal of a physical conversion, not a wall-time gain. This review does not rerun these checks or infer timing from profiler duration/counts.
judgment.next_experiment: No additional full-model window or broader D2 search is necessary to justify keeping the baseline when a candidate has no demonstrated benefit. One bounded same-process actual-vocabulary BF16-Top1 versus Cast-to-F32-Top1 control can explain local cost if already prepared; it cannot establish end-to-end gain or no-regression. If it yields no material local saving, close this candidate, revert the consumer change, retain its semantic regression test and negative evidence. Do not increase repeated full-window sampling merely to obtain a favorable sign.

fairness_limits: All metrics retain the complete host-token phase endpoint, including current cold preparation/capture, submit/wait/read. Full decode excludes prefill but includes initial two decode captures; warm7-end excludes decode1..6 in both arms.

Peer retains official F32 intermediate/logits consumer work including 248320 F32 logits per phase; Hyle BF16 boundary arithmetic differs. This is actual consumer-path comparison, not identical intermediate precision.
Long window uses 128 prompt plus127 repeated/truncated fixed decode inputs; matching predicted IDs is not free generation or quality acceptance.
Retained normal progress/graph logging and coarse peer memory snapshots exist; no new D1 buckets/profiler/external sampler/build within timing windows.
Logical read/write byte reductions are not measured DRAM bytes. Kernel/event counts and accumulated profiler durations are not additive wall-time savings.
The separate software profiler warns of unsupported driver fallback and software tracing; it is only structural evidence here.

bandwidth_review.scope: Read-only reconciliation of retained historical counters/hotspots with the one just-completed Top1 isolation; zero new GPU/build/profiler.
bandwidth_review.conclusion: Historical sampled large projections are strongly DRAM constrained; this dilutes the whole-step significance of tiny suffix savings. It does not prove every current kernel or the entire decode is DRAM-saturated, and it does not explain or establish the candidate full-model slowdown.

head_hardware_counter.meaning: This one sampled carrier reached97.55% of NCU sustained DRAM peak and491.223GB/s total measured DRAM traffic. This is evidence of little unused bandwidth in that sampled carrier, not an aggregate current-model measurement.
limits: Historical separate acquisition, seven kernel-replay passes, uncontrolled caches/clocks. Backup bytes are replay bookkeeping, not kernel traffic.
Total measured DRAM read+write traffic is not useful-weight-only bytes. Hyle/peer intermediate types differ, and their counter processes were not simultaneous.

dual_ffn_hardware_counter.meaning: One selected N6144/K2048 dual gate/up carrier has low measured L2 hit0.89% and high92.71% DRAM utilization. Its actual read50,827,648B is close to the logical two-bank50,331,648B, consistent with streaming for this node; L2 throughput was32.02% of its own sustained peak.
limits: 92.71% includes measured writes. Read-only rate407.691GB/s is below the466.797GB/s read+write rate; do not call useful-weight reads92.71% peak.

Five replay passes and shared L2/DRAM prevent weight-only or full-model attribution. The separate local-space probe found zero local load/store sectors, while DRAM writes changed; no extra dense intermediate or spill cause is proved.

cache_size_and_negative_optimization.meaning: The old three-bank row-tiling experiment exceeds36MiB L2 and showed equal stream medians despite fewer CTAs. This is a prior negative result, not a new candidate and not a universal cache-residency proof.

role_geometry_not_physical_traffic.meaning: Historical whole-model trace attributes about92.4% of summed kernel elapsed to projections. Head+gate/up+down are75.19% of logical weights. A one-token BF16 matrix-vector dot has about1 arithmetic operation per logical weight byte by2NK operations/2NK weightbytes, before other traffic; this is geometric reasoning, not a measured whole-model roofline.
limits: 3,762,552,832 logical weightbytes per step is tensor geometry, not an aggregate DRAM byte counter. No whole-model DRAM saturation or ideal tokens/s is inferred.
Projection share is a kernel-duration denominator, not unprofiled end-to-end wall share; traces are historical software-instrumented processes.

launch_latency_and_required_other_work.meaning: Most observed graph-interior time is occupied by actual kernels/copies. Required norm/gating/residual/GDN/attention/rounding work and host token completion exist outside projection intervals. Few-kernel savings must be measured by time, not count.
